correctness.rationale: For the finite rook graph K_p square K_q (2<=p<=q), the initially unobserved region is exactly I x J where I,J are unused rows and columns. If both |I|,|J|>=2, each observed neighbor has zero or at least two unobserved neighbors, preventing any force. If either |I|<=1 or |J|<=1, any remaining unobserved vertex has a forcing neighbor, so all are reached. This proves r(S)>=p-1 OR c(S)>=q-1, including p=2 and empty set. Counting failing sets by their exact occupied row/column supports gives the stated bipartite edge-cover inclusion-exclusion polynomial. Minimal size p-1 and coefficients p*q^(p-1) when p<q, or 2*p*p^(p-1)-p^2*(p-1)! when p=q, follow by overlapping row/column transversals. Maximal failing sets are full (p-2)x(q-2) rectangles, giving the sharp degree cutoff. Independent forcing simulation versus support criterion found n subsets 256 (2x4), 512 (3x3), 4096 (3x4), 65536 (4x4), with failing counts 1,10,31,317, matching all coefficients.
